t_reason_check: T1-038 (evidence/books/t-items-T1-w2.md:249-259) deleted the 2C-14/L11 case (before tests/work-graph/S2C-lines-failure.test.ts:186-197) because it 'only reaches [the branch] by rewriting the read-back content', citing slice-2C-SPEC.md:1053 ('defensive, no test required') and :1278 (never rewrite stored records). The premise is false for these lines: a Run end writes the ended Run and the Session occupancy release in ONE commit (src/core/work-graph/tasks/execution-entry-service.ts:1908-1915 calls claimEffectRecords :877-925, whose returned Session record is the release; src/core/work-graph/state/run-machine.ts:2008-2019; src/core/work-graph/state/session-availability.ts:779-786), while the reader takes the head Session in one read (src/core/work-graph/views/work-line-reader.ts:344, single-key readMany at :628) and the occupancy Run in a later read (:1064-1073). A real end committed between those two reads yields exactly the ended-but-occupied pair at :364-366. The same T item converted RD-8 to a commit gate for the same reason and accepted that a read-Session/read-Lease race is not tampering (tests/work-graph/S2C-lines-failure.test.ts:198-215); the T5x premise contradicts that ruling. No after-T test asserts source_moving on the line path: the only surviving assertions are the count path (tests/work-graph/S2C-lines-counts.test.ts:45) and the executions-page path (tests/work-graph/S2C-lines-page.test.ts:173), both different code. The deleted double forced the ended pair on both passes; the reachable single-race version asserts the healed row (problem null) and a reachable two-race version asserts source_moving, so the lines are not tamper-only either way.

Still concurrency, not tampering; the before case asserted exactly this through a read double.

restore: Target tests/work-graph/S2C-lines-failure.test.ts, adding completedEvent to its existing import from tests/helpers/S2C-L-runs-support.js, reusing its A3 read gate (:201-215) and the real services. One-race case (A2-059/060/061/062): `const f = await lineFixture(); const goal = await f.addGoal('g14-t5x-reread', [{ taskId: 'w', title: 'W task' }]); const head = (await f.createSession('s14-t5x-reread')).ref; const claim = await f.claim('w', head, goal);` (tests/helpers/S2C-L-line-support.ts:350) `await f.runs.enter(claim.claim);` (tests/helpers/S2C-L-runs-support.ts:136) `const headKey = canonicalJson({ aggregateType: 'Session', projectId: head.projectId, sessionId: head.sessionId } as unknown as JsonValue); let headReads = 0; const gated = { ...f.records, async readMany(keys: readonly string[]) { const read = await f.records.readMany(keys); if (keys.length === 1 && keys[0] === headKey) { headReads += 1; if (headReads === 1) await f.runs.recordResult(claim.claim, completedEvent(claim.claim, 't5x-reread')); } return read; } };` (recordResult :153, completedEvent :454) `const list = ready(await f.readerWith(gated).listWorkLines(f.ctx, { workspace: f.base.scope })); const row = rowOf(list.rows, head);` Assert `expect(headReads).toBe(2)` (the first pass saw the stale head with the Run occupied, the second pass reread and healed), `expect(row).toBeDefined()`, `expect(row?.problem).toBeNull()`. Add the same call once as `f.readerWith(gated2, 100)` on a fresh fixture so the :368 explicit-budget operand is exercised too. Two-race case for :493 arm 0 (fresh fixture): goal with tasks 'w' and 'w2'; claim+enter Run A on 'w'; the gate counts single-key head reads and on read 1 does `await f.runs.recordResult(a.claim, completedEvent(a.claim, 't5x-a'))`, then `const b = await f.claim('w2', head, goal); await f.runs.enter(b.claim);`; on read 2 it does `await f.runs.recordResult(b.claim, completedEvent(b.claim, 't5x-b'))`. Then assert `expect(headReads).toBe(2)`, `expect(row?.problem).toMatchObject({ code: 'source_moving' })`, `expect(row?.status.bucket).toBeNull()`. Both cases write only through the real claim/entry/result owners between reader awaits, the same seam RD-8 already uses; no stored record is rewritten and no read is faked.
